cues.en: The most straightforward metric is mean absolute error or MAE.
cues.zh: 最直接的指標，是平均絕對誤差，簡稱 MAE。

cues.en: Here is the fancy, mathematical equation for how to compute it.
cues.zh: 這是計算它的數學公式，看起來很厲害。

cues.en: It's not as complicated as it looks.
cues.zh: 其實沒看起來那麼複雜。

cues.en: So, let's break it down.
cues.zh: 來拆解一下。

cues.en: Let's say we have n ratings in our test set that we want to evaluate, for each rating we can call the rating or system predicts y, and the rating the user actually gave x.
cues.zh: 假設測試集中有 n 筆要評估的評分。對每筆評分，將系統預測的評分稱為 y，使用者實際給的評分稱為 x。

cues.en: Just take the absolute value of the difference between the two, to measure the error for that rating prediction.
cues.zh: 取兩者差的絕對值，就是這筆評分預測的誤差。

cues.en: It's literally just the difference between the predicted rating and the actual rating.
cues.zh: 真的就只是預測評分與實際評分的差。

cues.en: We sum those errors up across all n ratings in our test set, and divide by n to get the average, or mean.
cues.zh: 將測試集中全部 n 筆評分的誤差加總，再除以 n，取得平均值。

cues.en: So mean absolute error is exactly that, the mean or average absolute values of each error in rating predictions.
cues.zh: 所以平均絕對誤差，就是每筆評分預測誤差的絕對值的平均。

cues.en: Remember error is bad, so you want the lowest MAE score you can get, not the highest.
cues.zh: 記得，誤差越大越不好，因此 MAE 要越低越好，不是越高越好。

cues.en: Let's look at a simple example.
cues.zh: 看個簡單範例。

cues.en: Let's say we just have four ratings in our test set.
cues.zh: 假設測試集中只有四筆評分。

cues.en: On the first one our recommender system predicted a rating of five when the actual rating was three.
cues.zh: 第一筆，推薦系統預測五顆星，實際卻是三顆星。

cues.en: The absolute error in this case is two.
cues.zh: 這裡的絕對誤差是二。

cues.en: We just do that for every rating, add them all up and divide by four.
cues.zh: 對每筆評分都這樣做，加總後除以四。

cues.en: So the MAE score in this case is 1.5.
cues.zh: 因此，這個例子的 MAE 是 1.5。

cues.en: It's just that simple.
cues.zh: 就是這麼簡單。

cues.en: A slightly more fancy way to measure accuracy is root mean square error or RMSE.
cues.zh: 稍微進階一點的準確程度衡量方式，是均方根誤差，簡稱 RMSE。

cues.en: This is a more popular metric for a few reasons, but one is that it penalizes you more when your rating prediction is way off, and penalizes you less when you are reasonably close.
cues.zh: 這個指標更受歡迎，有幾個原因，其中之一是，預測偏差很大時懲罰較重，相當接近時懲罰較輕。

cues.en: The difference is that instead of summing up the absolute values of each rating prediction error, we sum up the squares of the rating prediction errors instead.
cues.zh: 差異是，不將每筆評分預測誤差的絕對值加總，而是改為加總每個誤差的平方。

cues.en: Taking the square ensures we end up with positive numbers, like absolute values do, and it also inflates the penalty for larger errors.
cues.zh: 平方和絕對值一樣，能確保結果是正數，同時會加重大誤差的懲罰。

cues.en: When we're done we take the square root to get back to a number that makes sense.
cues.zh: 最後再開平方根，回到有意義的數值尺度。

cues.en: So again, you can just take the name of the metric literally, root means that we take the square root of the whole thing when we are done, mean refers to an average, and square error is the square
cues.zh: 同樣地，直接照指標名稱理解即可：「根」代表最後對整體開平方根，「均」指平均，「平方誤差」就是每筆

cues.en: of each individual rating prediction error.
cues.zh: 評分預測誤差的平方。

cues.en: Let's walk through that same example.
cues.zh: 用同一個例子算一次。

cues.en: In the first rating in our test set The error between the predicted rating of five and the actual rating of three is two, and the square of that error is four.
cues.zh: 測試集第一筆，預測五顆星，實際三顆星，誤差是二，誤差的平方就是四。

cues.en: We just keep doing that for each rating in our test set and add them all up, then divide by the number of ratings, take the square root, and this time we end up with 1.87.
cues.zh: 對測試集每筆評分都這樣做並加總，再除以評分筆數、開平方根，這次得到 1.87。

cues.en: That's higher than the MAE score for this same data, of 1.5, because it's penalizing us hard for predicting a rating of four on an item that the user hated, with a rating of one.
cues.zh: 比相同資料的 MAE 1.5 更高，因為使用者很討厭、只給一顆星的項目，我們卻預測四顆星，受到了較重的懲罰。

cues.en: Again remember high RMSEs are bad, you want low error scores, not high ones.
cues.zh: 再次記得，RMSE 高是壞事，我們要低誤差，不是高誤差。

cues.en: Now like we said, accuracy isn't really measuring what we want recommender systems to do, actual people couldn't care less what your system thinks you should have rated some movie you already saw and rated.
cues.zh: 如同前面所說，準確程度並不是真正衡量推薦系統該做的事。真實使用者根本不在乎，系統認為他應該給某部已看過並評分的電影幾顆星。

cues.en: Rating predictions themselves are really a limited value, you don't really care if my system thinks you'll rate up three stars, you care mostly about what my system thinks about the best movies
cues.zh: 評分預測本身的價值其實有限。你並不在意我的系統認為你會給《天外奇蹟》三顆星，而是主要在意系統認為

cues.en: for you to go see are and that's a very different problem.
cues.zh: 有哪些最適合你去看的好電影，而這是截然不同的問題。

cues.en: So how do we end up focusing on accuracy and RMSE scores in the field of recommender system research?
cues.zh: 那麼，為什麼推薦系統研究領域會專注於準確程度與 RMSE 分數？

cues.en: Well, a lot of it dates back to 2006, when Netflix offered a one million dollar prize to the first person or group to achieve a 10 percent improvement on Netflix's own RMSE score on a data set
cues.zh: 很大一部分可以追溯到 2006 年，當時 Netflix 懸賞一百萬美元，給第一個能在它公開的

cues.en: of movie ratings it made public.
cues.zh: 電影評分資料集上，將 Netflix 原有 RMSE 改善 10% 的個人或團隊。

cues.en: This was called the Netflix prize, and that million dollar prize spurred a lot of research into recommender systems.
cues.zh: 這就是 Netflix Prize，一百萬美元獎金促進了大量推薦系統研究。

cues.en: Since the prize was based on achieving low RMSE scores, that's what everybody focused on, and that focus has rippled through time, even today.
cues.zh: 由於獎金取決於降低 RMSE，所有人都專注於此，這種影響一直延續到今天。

cues.en: And to be fair, there's not a lot of ways to measure a recommender system given only historical data to work with.
cues.zh: 公平地說，如果只有歷史資料可用，衡量推薦系統的方法確實不多。

cues.en: Ideally, you want to measure how real people react to recommendations for things they've never seen before, and you just can't do that offline.
cues.zh: 理想上，你想衡量真實使用者對從未看過的新項目推薦的反應，而離線根本做不到。

cues.en: If you're curious, the prize was awarded in 2009 to a team called BellKor and we'll talk about how they did it later on.
cues.zh: 如果好奇，這筆獎金在 2009 年頒給名為 BellKor 的團隊，稍後會談他們如何做到。

cues.en: But Netflix didn't actually end up using their research because they realized that RMSE just doesn't matter much in the real world.
cues.zh: 但 Netflix 最後並沒有實際採用這項研究，因為他們發現，RMSE 在真實世界其實沒那麼重要。

cues.en: What does matter is which movies you put in front of users in a top-end recommender list and how those users react to those movies when they see them recommended.
cues.zh: 真正重要的是，Top-N 推薦清單把哪些電影放到使用者面前，以及使用者看到這些推薦時，對電影有什麼反應。
